transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-20 15:00 UTC - Duration 47m - Attendees: Alex Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jon Wu (Redwood Solutions), Dr. Maya Singh (Orthosys), Ethan Cole (Orthosys), Lara Kim (Orthosys), Tom Reyes (Orthosys CTO)

00:00 Alex (AE): Okay hi everyone thanks for joining, we're, we're excited to learn about what Orthosys is building. quick intro from our side, I'm Alex Carter, AE for healthcare and regulated verticals, with me is Priya our solutions engineer and Jon on the solutions team.
00:12 Dr. Maya Singh: Hi, Maya here. we run the ML team, we're building an assistive clinical summarization pipeline and need pretty tight p95 SLA for streaming notes.
00:22 Ethan Cole: Ethan, platform, I'll own infra questions. we need to know if Redwood hosted can meet p95 200ms for the short prompts and about 1.2s for 512-token streaming p95, and also how throughput scales when we have 40-100 concurrent users.
00:36 Priya (SE): Great, thanks. quick clarifying q: those p95 numbers are for end-to-end from user keystroke to first token and then final? or are you measuring server-side token emission?
00:46 Dr. Maya Singh: We measure client-side to first token for streaming; for full response p95 we're targeting under 1.2s for 512 tokens, but first token should be <250ms ideally for snappy UX.
00:58 Alex: Perfect, that's helpful. can you share the typical prompt lengths and whether you're doing function-calling or structured output?
01:06 Dr. Maya Singh: Typical prompt is ~80-120 tokens with some context from EHR, then we stream - partial tokens - structured JSON at the end. no heavy function calls but we do metadata lookups.
01:18 Priya: Okay. just to set expectations, for Hosted API in our catalog with H100-backed instances we commonly see first-token p50 under 100ms but p95 is more workload dependent; for 512 token streams with continuous batching, p95 can be sub 1.2s if batching and KV cache fit. for Dedicated we can tune batch sizes and isolate GPUs for more predictable p95.
01:39 Ethan: when you say H100-backed, is that the Redwood dedicated nodes or hosted? we have regulatory needs so private VPC is in play but we want to understand cost/timing.
01:48 Alex: H100 or A100 depending on region and model. hosted uses a mix of cloud GPUs, Dedicated can be pinned to H100s. Private (VPC/on-prem) we can do on customer-approved hardware, yes.
01:58 Lara Kim: Security check - we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, audit logs with per-team isolation and KMS integration for keys. also data residency in eu-west for some patients.
02:09 Alex: we are SOC2 Type II, SSO via SAML/OIDC, and offer KMS/HSM integrations; we can share the security pack after.
02:17 Tom Reyes: what's the latency tradeoff between quantized models and fp16/higher precision? we need accurate clinical outputs so quality matters.
02:25 Priya: quantization saves cost and can reduce token/sec, but sometimes increases p95 depending on kernel. we recommend running quality evals. for many of the decoder-only models, int8 quant gives ~1.2x throughput improvement but sometimes small PPL changes.
02:38 Jon: also caching - if you have repeated prefixes from the EHR we can do prefix/KV caching to shave off a few hundred ms for repeated contexts. note: sometimes the transcript text shows KV cash in the auto-note, sorry transcription quirk.
02:52 Dr. Maya Singh: good point. and concurrency: we expect 20-40 concurrent writers during peak and occasional bursts to 100. sustained avg is around 35.
03:02 Priya: that helps. are you doing token-level streaming to clients or batching server-side then flushing?
03:08 Ethan: token-level streaming. front-end expects partial tokens as they generate.
03:12 Priya: okay streaming is more sensitive to tail latency since user sees first tokens quickly; our runtime supports streaming with continuous batching and KV cache, but at high concurrency we may fall back to slightly higher batch sizes to maintain throughput.
03:24 Alex: buyers often test two things: p95 first token and sustained token/sec under concurrency. For a pilot we usually instrument both: synthetic token/sec bench and a replay of your real traces.
03:35 Dr. Maya Singh: we'd like Redwood to run a 48h pilot with our trace, measuring p50/p95/p99 for first token and full responses.
03:42 Alex: absolutely, we can do that. Priya will define a perf script.
03:45 Priya: we'll ask for a sample of traces (anonymized), target concurrency matrix (20,40,100), and target prompt/resp sizes (80/512). we'll run hosted and dedicated configs: hosted baseline + dedicated pinned H100 + private (if you provide infra).
03:58 Lara Kim: how do you handle audit logs and key access? we need proof for auditors.
04:03 Alex: we provide audit logs, per-request metadata, and KMS integration; can deliver an architecture doc showing key rotation and HSM path. we'll send the SOC2 pack.
04:12 Ethan: pricing - Dedicated monthly commit vs hosted usage - can you give roughs now?
04:16 Alex: roughly, hosted per-token for this model class is X cents token (we'll follow up with exact), Dedicated is subscription + infra cost with a lower per-token strip; we'll send a tailored pricing doc.
04:25 Dr. Maya Singh: any known customers in medtech? references?
04:28 Alex: yes a couple - we can share sanitized references and an H100 benchmark spreadsheet.
04:32 Tom Reyes: technical: do you support pinned model versions and rolling canaries? our release process needs deterministic rollouts.
04:38 Priya: yes per-route model pinning and rollouts with automatic fallback policies, canary and A/B.
04:43 Jon: one more comment on streaming benchmarks: token/sec numbers vary a lot by sequence length; short prompts often have higher token/sec but tail p95 can hurt for many concurrent short requests. so we'll include variable-length runs.
04:57 Dr. Maya Singh: do you have published p95 numbers for 512 token streams on H100?
05:02 Priya: we have internal numbers, we'll share the spreadsheet. typical p95 for 512 tokens on H100 for our tested models is ~0.9-1.1s end-to-end in hosted with moderate concurrency, Dedicated can tighten that to ~0.7-0.9s depending on pipeline and KV cache hit rate. note: these are ballparks and vary by quantization and model variant.
05:24 Ethan: what about cold-starts and autoscaling - we can't have cold-starts add 2-3s on critical flows.
05:32 Alex: Dedicated has reserved GPUs so cold-starts are minimal; hosted routes use warm pools and pre-warming strategies. autoscale policies can be tuned; we'll propose a config to avoid cold penalties.
05:44 Lara Kim: for private on-prem, what about ops burden? we don't want a huge lift.
05:49 Priya: Private includes a control plane we manage or optionally you manage; we provide deployment ansible/k8s manifests and an onboarding runbook. some customers choose managed private for less ops.
05:59 Dr. Maya Singh: ok, next steps?
06:02 Alex: recap: we'll send SOC2 and security docs, pricing, benchmark spreadsheet; Priya will define pilot scope and perf scripts; Orthosys will provide anonymized traces and compliance questionnaire. Pilot kickoff next Tue proposed.
06:14 Tom Reyes: sounds good. thanks everyone.
06:18 Alex: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites and links.

Notes: transcript includes occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache) and speaker label glitches typical of auto-transcribe.
